claim: KCNQ1 voltage-gated potassium channels coassemble with KCNE1 β-subunits to generate the IKs current in the heart.
source: In the heart, KCNQ1 voltage-gated potassium channels coassemble with KCNE1 β-subunits to generate the IKs current (Barhanin et al., 1996; Sanguinetti et al., 1996)
evidence: Supported by citations to Barhanin et al., 1996 and Sanguinetti et al., 1996

claim: IKs current is important for maintenance of stable heart rhythms.
source: In the heart, KCNQ1 voltage-gated potassium channels coassemble with KCNE1 β-subunits to generate the IKs current (Barhanin et al., 1996; Sanguinetti et al., 1996), an important current for maintenance of stable heart rhythms.
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge about cardiac electrophysiology

claim: KCNE1 significantly modulates the gating, permeation, and pharmacology of KCNQ1.
source: KCNE1 significantly modulates the gating, permeation, and pharmacology of KCNQ1 (Wrobel et al., 2012; Sun et al., 2012; Abbott, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wrobel et al., 2012; Sun et al., 2012; Abbott, 2014

claim: The changes induced by KCNE1 are essential for the physiological role of IKs.
source: These changes are essential for the physiological role of IKs (Silva and Rudy, 2005)
evidence: Supported by citation to Silva and Rudy, 2005

claim: KCNE1 alters the state-dependent interactions that functionally couple the voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) to the pore.
source: Here we provide evidence of such a mechanism, whereby, KCNE1 alters the state-dependent interactions that functionally couple the voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) to the pore.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript

claim: Voltage-gated ion channels consist of four voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) surrounding a central pore.
source: These channels consist of four voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) surrounding a central pore.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about voltage-gated ion channels

claim: In voltage-gated potassium (Kv) channels, the structure results from the tetrameric assembly of Kv-α subunits, each containing six transmembrane-spanning segments (S1–S6).
source: In voltage-gated potassium (Kv) channels, this structure results from the tetrameric assembly of Kv-α subunits, each of which contain six transmembrane-spanning segments (S1–S6).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about Kv channels

claim: S1–S4 of each subunit forms a voltage-sensing domain (VSD).
source: S1–S4 of each subunit forms a voltage-sensing domain (VSD)
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about Kv channels

claim: S5–S6's from all four subunits form the pore.
source: S5–S6's from all four subunits form the pore.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about Kv channels

claim: At depolarized voltages, the forces of the membrane electric field on positively charged residues promotes the outward displacement of S4 toward its activated state.
source: At depolarized voltages, the forces of the membrane electric field on these positively charged residues promotes the outward displacement of S4 toward its activated state (Papazian et al., 1995; Larsson et al., 1996; Silva et al., 2009; Wu et al., 2010a; Delemotte et al., 2011; Jensen et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: The pore contains the ion permeation pathway that can be opened and closed by the reorientation of the intracellular portions of the S6 helices.
source: The pore contains the ion permeation pathway that can be opened and closed by the reorientation of the intracellular portions of the S6 helices (Liu et al., 1997; Webster et al., 2004; del Camino and Yellen, 2001; Jiang et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Interactions between the VSDs and the pore couple the activation of the VSD to the opening of the pore, resulting in a voltage-gated conductance.
source: Critical to voltage-dependent gating are the interactions between the VSDs and the pore, which couple the activation of the VSD to the opening of the pore, resulting in a voltage-gated conductance (Chen et al., 2001; Lu et al., 2001, 2002; Long et al., 2005; Lee et al., 2009; Zaydman et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Hodgkin and Huxley empirically derived a model for the K+ conductance in which a transmembrane pathway is gated by four voltage-dependent particles.
source: In their pioneering work on the action potential of the squid giant axon, Hodgkin and Huxley empirically derived a model for the K+ conductance in which a transmembrane pathway is gated by four voltage-dependent particles (Hodgkin and Huxley, 1952).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hodgkin and Huxley, 1952

claim: Current Kv channel models assume that VSD activation and pore opening are two-state (i.e., all or none) processes.
source: The legacy of the Hogdkin and Huxley model can still be found in the current Kv channel models, which assume that (1) VSD activation and pore opening are two-state (i.e., all or none) processes
evidence: This is a statement about the assumptions in current models, based on inference from the literature

claim: Current Kv channel models assume that gating and permeation are independent so that the VSD conformation changes the probability of pore opening, but does not affect the properties of the open pore.
source: The legacy of the Hogdkin and Huxley model can still be found in the current Kv channel models, which assume that (1) VSD activation and pore opening are two-state (i.e., all or none) processes and (2) gating and permeation are independent so that the VSD conformation changes the probability of pore opening, but does not affect the properties of the open pore.
evidence: This is a statement about the assumptions in current models, based on inference from the literature

claim: VSD activation actually occurs in a series of stepwise transitions due to salt bridge interactions between the basic residues on S4 and acidic residues on S1 and S2, which define resting, intermediate, and activated states.
source: Computational and experimental studies have demonstrated that VSD activation actually occurs in a series of stepwise transitions due to salt bridge interactions between the basic residues on S4 and acidic residues on S1 and S2, which define resting, intermediate, and activated states (Papazian et al., 1995; Tiwari-Woodruff et al., 1997; Wu et al., 2010a; Delemotte et al., 2011; Jensen et al., 2012; Lacroix et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Recordings of single channel currents from Kv channels revealed multiple open states discernable by their different conductance levels.
source: With regards to pore opening, recordings of single channel currents from Kv channels revealed multiple open states discernable by their different conductance levels (Chapman et al., 1997)
evidence: Supported by citation to Chapman et al., 1997

claim: Both the intermediate and fully-activated states of the VSD yielded robust pore-opening in KCNQ1 channels.
source: In our present study of KCNQ1 (Kv7.1, KvLQT1) channels, we found that both the intermediate and fully-activated states of the VSD yielded robust pore-opening.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study, supported by experimental data

claim: The intermediate-open and activated-open states had different permeation and pharmacological properties.
source: Remarkably, the intermediate-open and activated-open states had different permeation and pharmacological properties revealing that VSD-pore interactions determine both open probability and open conformation, demonstrating that gating and permeation are not independent.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study, supported by experimental data

claim: VSD-pore interactions determine both open probability and open conformation, demonstrating that gating and permeation are not independent.
source: Remarkably, the intermediate-open and activated-open states had different permeation and pharmacological properties revealing that VSD-pore interactions determine both open probability and open conformation, demonstrating that gating and permeation are not independent.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study, supported by experimental data and inference

claim: KCNQ1 channels generate currents with very different properties as a result of tissue specific expression of KCNE family accessory subunits.
source: KCNQ1 channels generate currents with very different properties as a result of tissue specific expression of KCNE family accessory subunits (Abbott, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Abbott, 2014

claim: Channels formed by KCNQ1 and KCNE1 subunits are responsible for the slow-delayed rectifier potassium current, IKs.
source: In the heart, channels formed by KCNQ1 and KCNE1 subunits are responsible for the slow-delayed rectifier potassium current, IKs (Barhanin et al., 1996; Sanguinetti et al., 1996)
evidence: Supported by citations to Barhanin et al., 1996 and Sanguinetti et al., 1996

claim: IKs plays a critical role in limiting action potential duration when beta-adrenergic tone is elevated.
source: In the heart, channels formed by KCNQ1 and KCNE1 subunits are responsible for the slow-delayed rectifier potassium current, IKs (Barhanin et al., 1996; Sanguinetti et al., 1996), which plays a critical role in limiting action potential duration when beta-adrenergic tone is elevated.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiac electrophysiology

claim: A large set of loss-of-function mutations of KCNQ1 or KCNE1 have been associated with Long QT Syndrome and result in an elevated risk of fatal arrhythmias during times of stress.
source: The importance of this response is highlighted by a large set of loss-of-function mutations of KCNQ1 or KCNE1 that have been associated with Long QT Syndrome and result in an elevated risk of fatal arrhythmias during times of stress (Paavonen et al., 2001; Schwartz et al., 2001; Hedley et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Paavonen et al., 2001; Schwartz et al., 2001; Hedley et al., 2009

claim: KCNE1 coassembly dramatically alters voltage-dependence, current kinetics, inactivation, current amplitude, single channel conductance, selectivity, and pharmacology of KCNQ1 channels.
source: Although KCNE1 is a small, single-membrane-spanning peptide, its coassembly dramatically alters every physiologically relevant property of the KCNQ1 channel: voltage-dependence, current kinetics, inactivation, current amplitude, single channel conductance, selectivity, and pharmacology (Wrobel et al., 2012; Sun et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wrobel et al., 2012 and Sun et al., 2012

claim: Some groups have argued that KCNE1 alters VSD activation.
source: The mechanism of how KCNE1 modulates KCNQ1 has been a longstanding topic of debate with several groups arguing that KCNE1 alters VSD activation (Nakajo and Kubo, 2007; Ruscic et al., 2013)
evidence: Supported by citations to Nakajo and Kubo, 2007 and Ruscic et al., 2013

claim: Some groups have argued that KCNE1 alters pore opening.
source: several other groups arguing that KCNE1 alters pore opening (Rocheleau and Kobertz, 2008; Osteen et al., 2010)
evidence: Supported by citations to Rocheleau and Kobertz, 2008 and Osteen et al., 2010

claim: Some reports claim that KCNE1 directly contributes to the inner structure of the pore.
source: and several reports claiming that KCNE1 directly contributes to the inner structure of the pore (Wang et al., 1996; Tai and Goldstein, 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wang et al., 1996 and Tai and Goldstein, 1998

claim: Previous mechanisms are not able to simultaneously account for the effects of KCNE1 on gating and the observed changes in permeation and pharmacology.
source: However, these mechanisms are not able to simultaneously account for the effects of KCNE1 on gating and the observed changes in permeation and pharmacology.
evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' analysis of the literature

claim: VSD activation in KCNQ1 occurs in two resolvable steps through a stable intermediate state.
source: First, we found that VSD activation occurs in two resolvable steps through a stable intermediate state.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study, supported by experimental data

claim: The intermediate-state of the VSD is sufficient to promote KCNQ1 channel opening, resulting in both intermediate-open and activated-open states.
source: Second, we observed that the intermediate-state of the VSD is sufficient to promote KCNQ1 channel opening, resulting in both intermediate-open and activated-open states.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study, supported by experimental data

claim: The intermediate-open and activated-open states have different permeation and pharmacological properties.
source: Third, we observed that the intermediate-open and activated-open states have different permeation and pharmacological properties.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study, supported by experimental data

claim: Coexpression of KCNE1 prevented the intermediate-open state and changed the properties of the activated-open state.
source: We found that coexpression of KCNE1 prevented the intermediate-open state and changed the properties of the activated-open state.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study, supported by experimental data

claim: KCNE1 changes how the VSD and pore interact.
source: The apparent decoupling of pore opening from the resting to intermediate transition of the VSD suggested that KCNE1 changes how the VSD and pore interact.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental observations

claim: Changing the VSD-pore interactions directly via a single point mutation also prevented the intermediate-open state and modified the properties of the activated-open state.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, changing the VSD-pore interactions directly via a single point mutation also prevented the intermediate-open state and modified the properties of the activated-open state.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study, supported by experimental data

claim: The effects of KCNE1 on VSD-pore interactions are sufficient to simultaneously explain most of the changes in activation gating without any direct impacts on VSD activation or pore opening.
source: Using a kinetic model, we demonstrated that the effects of KCNE1 on VSD-pore interactions, as suggested by our data, are sufficient to simultaneously explain most of the changes in activation gating without any direct impacts on VSD activation or pore opening.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study, supported by kinetic modeling

claim: Altering VSD-pore interactions is likely the primary mechanism through which KCNE1 modulates KCNQ1.
source: Therefore we conclude that altering VSD-pore interactions is likely the primary mechanism through which KCNE1 modulates KCNQ1.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, based on experimental data and modeling

claim: A fluorophore attached to the S3–S4 linker of pseudo-WT KCNQ1 channels reports on conformational changes associated with VSD activation.
source: In our VCF records, a fluorophore attached to the S3–S4 linker of pseudo-WT KCNQ1 channels (with mutations C214A/G219C/C331A) reports on conformational changes associated with VSD activation (Figure 1A–H, green), while the ionic currents report the opening of the pore (Figure 1A–H, black) (Osteen et al., 2010; Zaydman et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Osteen et al., 2010 and Zaydman et al., 2013

claim: Multiple components of the fluorescence signals were observed for KCNQ1.
source: We observed multiple components of the fluorescence signals for KCNQ1 (Figure 1A–D)
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-D

claim: Multiple components of the fluorescence signals were observed for KCNQ1+KCNE1.

evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E-H and citation to Barro-Soria et al., 2014

claim: Most of the total change in fluorescence intensity was due to a fast component occurring at hyperpolarized voltages (Fmain).
source: Most of the total change in fluorescence intensity was due to a fast component occurring at hyperpolarized voltages (Fmain), but a small additional change was observed due to a slow component occurring at highly depolarized voltages (Fhigh).
evidence: Supported by experimental data

claim: A small additional change in fluorescence was observed due to a slow component occurring at highly depolarized voltages (Fhigh).
source: Most of the total change in fluorescence intensity was due to a fast component occurring at hyperpolarized voltages (Fmain), but a small additional change was observed due to a slow component occurring at highly depolarized voltages (Fhigh).
evidence: Supported by experimental data

claim: The FV-GV correlations were maintained in the presence of a KCNQ1 mutation, R243Q, that shifted the voltage dependence of channel opening.

claim: KCNQ1 current onset had two exponential components following the two timecourses of the fluorescence.

evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B-D

evidence: Supported by citations to Silva et al., 2009 and Wu et al., 2010a, and experimental data

claim: These interactions stabilize discrete resting, intermediate, and activated states of the VSD.

These interactions stabilize discrete resting, intermediate, and activated states.

claim: Homology models of KCNQ1 were built with the VSDs in states where E1 forms a salt bridge with R228 (R1), R231 (R2), or R237 (R4).

claim: R228 (R1), R231 (R2), and R237 (R4) are the three S4 arginines that are known to be critical for voltage-sensing in KCNQ1.

claim: MD simulations suggest that KCNQ1 channels can open when the VSDs assume intermediate or activated states.

claim: Mutating E1 to arginine (E1R) caused a severe loss of current in KCNQ1 channels.

evidence: Supported by citation to Wu et al., 2010a and experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: The loss of current from E1R mutation was partially rescued by a charge reversing (R to E) mutation at the R2 (E1R/R2E) or R4 (E1R/R4E) positions.

claim: KCNE1 suppresses the intermediate-open state and potentiates the activated-open state.
